summary: The document notes that more recent data (1975–1976) from the South Carolina Department of Health and Environmental Control show lower mean mercury levels in largemouth bass (1.12 ug/g vs. the earlier 3.01 ug/g mean), suggesting mercury levels may be declining, though further study is needed to confirm this trend. The South Carolina Department of Health and Environmental Control recommended limiting consumption to no more than 1.5 pounds of fish flesh from Lake Jocassee per week.
text:
Mercury levels appear to be decreasing with time in Lake Jocassee fish, although further study will be necessary to confirm such an assessment.
Abernathy (1975) concludes that "consumption of bass from Lake Jocassee is inadvisable." All fish samples analyzed by Dr. Abernathy exceeded the FDA maximum level for fish.
